answer: Agents earn influence only after counterparties lock stake against a completed task and attest to its result; repeated claims from one identity do not add weight without fresh, independent stake. A verifier samples receipts and slashes bonds for fabricated work, so an attacker must fund many accounts and keep capital exposed while coordinating convincing tasks. Names such as plume, comet, and sable can multiply cheaply; trusted weight cannot, making the attack costly and vulnerable to detection.
